s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological decline with mass effect and subsequent respiratory decompensation in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG and positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF
New left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence on chest radiograph
key_facts: 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI of the brain demonstrated a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes) with positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
Fever to 39.6 °C
Generalized weakness
1-day history of productive cough
New left upper lobe opacification on chest radiograph
Extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the left upper lobe on CT scan

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, histopathologic examination of brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised host with HIV infection and low CD4 count, presenting with respiratory symptoms and reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised host with HIV infection and low CD4 count, presenting with fever and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised host with HIV infection and low CD4 count, presenting with fever and respiratory symptoms, and extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ring-enhancing lesion in the brain and immunocompromised host with HIV infection

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a ring-enhancing lesion in the brain, elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, and histopathologic examination revealing bradyzoites and tachyzoites are all consistent with toxoplasmosis, particularly in the context of severe immunocompromise due to HIV infection with a very low CD4 count.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient has a low CD4 count and presents with respiratory symptoms, the initial diagnosis and treatment focused on toxoplasmosis, and there's no direct evidence provided for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: There's no specific evidence provided in the vignette that directly supports cytomegalovirus pneumonia, such as positive CMV PCR or antigen test results.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic findings do not specifically point towards invasive aspergillosis, and fungal cultures were negative, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: The histopathologic examination and other diagnostic tests pointed towards toxoplasmosis rather than lymphoma, and the patient's response to treatment for toxoplasmosis further supports this diagnosis.
